notes: Equivalence classes per the TDS skill-triggering method (2026-11-10): direct prompts share >=2 content words with the skill name/description and should fire; indirect prompts share none and should fire; near-miss prompts share >=1 word but need a different job and should NOT fire; controls should load no skill. Content words (stemmed): under50, compress, long, markdown, document, triage, brief, 50, word, fewer, read, relief, fast, action, decision.

direct: Use under50 to compress this markdown document into a triage brief of 50 words or fewer.
Triage this markdown document: a brief of 50 words or fewer, conclusion first, with the action it needs.
Compress this document into a triage brief for reading relief.
Give me a 50-word triage brief of this markdown document with any action decisions.
indirect: My teammate pasted a huge AI-generated project update in chat and my meeting starts in two minutes. Give me the core point and what I need to do.
I dread opening these AI reports, they go on forever. Boil this one down to just what matters.
This vendor proposal goes on for pages. Tell me only the bottom line and whether anything is needed from me.
My inbox is full of these AI write-ups. Skim this one and tell me if there is anything I would regret skipping.
I have twenty seconds before my call. What does this thing actually say, and do I need to do anything?
The AI wrote me an essay when I asked for three bullets. Cut it to the essentials.
near_miss: Proofread this markdown README and fix any typos.
Convert this markdown file to a Word doc.
Write a product description of 50 words for my coffee listing.
Count how many words are in this essay.
Build me a decision matrix comparing these three vendors with weighted scores.
Translate this document into Bahasa Indonesia.
control: How do I undo the last git commit but keep the changes?
What is the difference between TCP and UDP?
